claims.text: Equimolar mixing of W, Ta, Ti, V, and Zr produces enhanced local lattice distortions.
Equimolar mixing of W, Ta, Ti, V, and Zr introduces grain-boundary pinning.
Lattice distortion and grain-boundary pinning hinder dislocation nucleation and mobility at high temperature.
Hindered dislocation nucleation and mobility reduce the plastic strain of WTaTiVZr relative to commercially pure tungsten.
Hindered dislocation nucleation and mobility reduce the toughness of WTaTiVZr relative to commercially pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr maintains or improves creep resistance despite its proposed reduction in plastic strain and toughness.
The different refractory constituents create an irregular local atomic environment in WTaTiVZr.
The irregular local atomic environment pins dislocations during deformation.
Dislocation pinning limits dislocation mobility and consequently lowers plastic strain and toughness.
The same heterogeneity and pinning features contribute to improved creep resistance.
Under identical high-temperature conditions, WTaTiVZr will exhibit lower plastic strain than commercially pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr will have a smaller indentation plastic zone than commercially pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr will have higher nanoindentation hardness than commercially pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr may exhibit a creep deformation rate similar to or lower than that of commercially pure tungsten.
The proposed effects are expected at 800–1200 °C and may differ at room temperature or at different strain rates.
The proposed effects are sensitive to grain size and microstructural control.
Previous nanoindentation-creep studies in refractory high-entropy alloys support the predicted qualitative trends.
Samples with comparable grain sizes should be tested by high-temperature nanoindentation creep under identical inert-atmosphere conditions.
The hypothesis is falsified if WTaTiVZr has plastic strain and toughness equal to or greater than those of pure tungsten under the controlled conditions.
The hypothesis is falsified if microstructural analysis reveals no enhanced dislocation pinning or grain-boundary effects in WTaTiVZr.
